sections.content: When a person does something to a thing, such as cooks it, buys it or reads it, that thing is the object, and in Hungarian the object takes the ending *-t*. *Anna főz levest.* means “Anna cooks soup.” The verb endings you know stay as they are: *főzök*, *főzöl*, *főz*. The object after *egy* or with no article takes *-t* in the same way: *Vásárolok egy almát.*

sections.title: After a vowel: just add -t (a and e become á and é)
After a consonant: learn each word
Linking vowels
sections.content: After a consonant, many words add a linking vowel before the *-t*: *-ot* after back vowels (*sajtot*), *-et* after front vowels (*tejet*). Some take the *-t* directly (*levest*), and two common ones shorten their long vowel: *vizet* and *kenyeret*. A final *-a* or *-e* lengthens before *-t*: *alma → almát*, *tea → teát*. Learn them as pairs.

*Van tej* only says the milk is there, so it has no *-t*. *Tejet vásárolok* says you do something to the milk, so it takes *-t*. In this unit the verbs are the ones you know, and the object is *egy* + noun or the bare noun.
